# Get started

vellumplot is a declarative, pipe-first grammar of graphics built on the
[vellum](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellum/) backend. You describe a
plot as an inspectable, serializable *spec*; nothing is drawn until the
spec is compiled into a vellum scene and rendered.

## Install

vellumplot compiles a Rust crate (inside `vellum`), so you need a Rust
toolchain (`cargo`/`rustc`) on your machine alongside R. With that in
place:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("r-vellum/vellumplot")
```

## A first plot

Start with
[`vplot()`](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumplot/reference/vplot.md) on
a data frame, then add a mark. Encodings (`x`, `y`, `color`, …) are
tidy-eval expressions evaluated against the data.

``` r

library(vellumplot)

vplot(mtcars) |>
  mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = hp) |>
  scale_color_continuous()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Printing a spec draws it into the plots pane (and embeds in a
knitr/Quarto chunk), like ggplot2.

## Layering marks

Add more marks to the same panel; scales train across every layer.

``` r

vplot(mtcars) |>
  mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>
  mark_smooth(x = wt, y = mpg)
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Faceting

Split into a grid of panels with shared or free scales.

``` r

vplot(mtcars) |>
  mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>
  facet_wrap(~cyl)
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## The spec is just data

Nothing is drawn until the spec is compiled.
[`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html) shows its structure
without rendering.

``` r

summary(vplot(mtcars) |> mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = hp))
#> <PlotSpec> 32x11 (11 columns), page 6x4 in
#> 
#> ── layers
#> • mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = hp)
```

## Rendering to a file

[`render_plot()`](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumplot/reference/render_plot.md)
writes the compiled scene; the format follows the file extension:
`.png`, `.svg`, `.pdf` or `.pptx`.

``` r

p <- vplot(mtcars) |> mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg)
render_plot(p, "cars.png")
```

The layout is solved once, by vellum, so the PNG, the SVG, the PDF and
the PowerPoint slide all share it.

### Saving to PowerPoint

A `.pptx` path writes a one-slide PowerPoint file of **editable shapes**
at the plot’s size. Every point, bar and line is a DrawingML shape,
every plain-text label a text box you can retype (math and haloed labels
are outlines), and each panel a named group you can ungroup, recolour or
move in PowerPoint. No other package is needed.

``` r

render_plot(p, "cars.pptx")
```

[`vellum::pptx_pages()`](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellum/reference/pptx_pages.html)
writes several plots as the slides of one deck, also without officer:

``` r

p2 <- vplot(mtcars) |> mark_histogram(x = mpg, bins = 10)
vellum::pptx_pages(list(p, p2), "deck.pptx")
```

To put a plot on a slide of your own deck, built with
[officer](https://davidgohel.github.io/officer/), wrap it in
[`vellum::as_dml()`](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellum/reference/as_dml.html)
and hand it to `officer::ph_with()`. The plot is laid out again at the
size of the placeholder, so its text keeps its point size and nothing is
stretched (`resize = FALSE` keeps the plot’s own size).

``` r

library(officer)

deck <- read_pptx() |>
  add_slide(layout = "Title and Content") |>
  ph_with("Fuel economy", location = ph_location_type("title")) |>
  ph_with(vellum::as_dml(p), location = ph_location_type("body"))
print(deck, target = "fuel.pptx")
```

Fonts are named, not embedded: PowerPoint uses the font vellum measured
the text with when the machine opening the deck has it, and substitutes
another when it doesn’t. `text = "outline"` (in
[`render_plot()`](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumplot/reference/render_plot.md),
`pptx_pages()` and `as_dml()`) writes glyph outlines instead, which look
the same everywhere but can’t be edited as text. DrawingML has no
clipping, blend modes or masks, so vellum cuts clipped geometry in
advance and draws the parts it can’t express (a blur, a blend mode) as a
picture, with a warning. vellum’s [PowerPoint
article](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellum/articles/powerpoint.html)
covers the details.

For many figures at once,
[`pdf_pages()`](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumplot/reference/pdf_pages.md)
and
[`render_all()`](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumplot/reference/render_all.md)
are covered in [Facets and
composition](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumplot/articles/facets-and-composition.html#multi-page-and-batch-output).

### Strings and documents

[`plot_svg()`](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumplot/reference/plot_svg.md)
returns the scene as an SVG string, and
[`plot_data_uri()`](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumplot/reference/plot_data_uri.md)
inlines a plot as a self-contained `data:` URI (vector by default, or
`format = "png"`) for an `<img>`, a Markdown image, or an email — no
separate file.

``` r

uri <- p |> plot_data_uri()          # data:image/svg+xml;base64,...
```

Inside a Quarto or R Markdown document you usually write nothing
special: a plot printed in a chunk adapts to the target — a crisp inline
**SVG** for HTML output, and the default vector/raster render for PDF or
Word.

In HTML the SVG fills the column at the plot’s own aspect. A chunk’s
`fig-width` / `fig-height` / `fig-asp` (`fig.width` / `fig.height` /
`fig.asp` in R Markdown) sizes the dimensions a plot was not given:
`vplot(df)` without `width` / `height` (or a composition of such plots)
is laid out at that size, and a chunk’s `fig-width` also caps how wide
it is shown, so a small figure stays small. A `fig-asp` alone sets the
height to the plot’s width times the aspect. A size passed to
[`vplot()`](https://r-vellum.github.io/vellumplot/reference/vplot.md) or
to the composition, even `width = 6, height = 4`, is kept (so is a
sparkline’s or a table’s), and the plot fills the column. Only values
the chunk changes count: a chunk value equal to the document’s default
(or the document-wide `fig-asp`) leaves plots as they are. A chunk’s
`out-width` sets the figure’s CSS width.
